messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — elevated 502/504 rate at edge mux in eu-west-1. surge started ~2m ago, error rate ~18% over 1m window :rotating_light:
jamie_oncall: i'm on it. switching pager to 'incident' — @megan_sre can you grab logs and confirm upstream error mix?
megan_sre: looking. quick summary: most 502s are TLS handshake failures to upstream model pool (tls: handshake timeout) + some 504s where request queueing hit proxy timeouts.
dmitry_eng: tagging in — any deploys or cert rotations in last 10m? 
lia_support: fielding customer reports, a handful of API keys seeing >30% failures, some 429s as clients retry. customers affected: two mid-market tenants on eu-west endpoints.
jamie_oncall: ok plan: 1) enable fallback routing to eu-west-standby (non-primary mux) 2) put affected upstream pool into degraded health so traffic shifts 3) open readonly status page note. megan, can you run fallback now?
megan_sre: running fallback command: 
```
# switch mux fallback route
redwoodctl route set --mux edge-eu-west --fallback edge-eu-west-standby --reason "tls-handshake-spike"
```
megan_sre: command accepted, propagating. watching metrics.
dmitry_eng: checking LB and TLS metrics: could be SNI mismatch with a subset of hosts after an automated cert renew. seeing handshake error spikes pinned to host header batch `model-v2-*.svc`
ben_platform: i can pause the cert-rotation job for that pool if you want; it's running in the background.
jamie_oncall: pause it. we don't want churn while we triage. ops-rotation: please notify infra rotation.
ops-rotation: paused cert-rotation job `cert-roller/eu-west` ✅.
lia_support: posting interim message to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated 5xx rates in EU West for API endpoints; routing mitigations are in progress. We'll update in 15m or sooner."
megan_sre: fallback applied, traffic to standby increased ~65% in 30s. error rate dropped to 4.2% overall. still seeing intermittent TLS timeouts for a small subset.
dmitry_eng: isolating subset by client IP/netblock; looks like some old clients using TLS1.0 fallback? weird. dumping a sample of failing headers: 
```
Host: model-v2-123.svc.redwood
User-Agent: redwood-client/1.2.0
TLS-Version: TLSv1.0
SNI: model-v2-123.svc.redwood
```
jamie_oncall: note: we should avoid killing primary pool until we confirm rollback path. recommended next step: 1) keep fallback for now 2) scale up standby by 2x 3) run health-checks on primary to see if it's cert-only or broader.
ben_platform: scaling standby +2 nodes now. ETA ~45s.
megan_sre: running health checks: primary pool instances responding to simple GET but failing at TLS handshake on longer-lived connections. suspect mTLS misconfiguration after rotation.
dmitry_eng: agree. i'll pull rotation logs and confirm what changed. if it's a cert chain ordering issue we can reapply previous cert bundle.
lia_support: customers responded: two tenants acknowledged degraded but accepted mitigation; one asked for ETA to full fix. I've escalated to account team.
jamie_oncall: handoff plan in 30m: if we're not at <1% overall errors, keep oncall and escalate to platform lead. for now, stay in this channel and log any customer-impact notes. set status page to "Partial outage - degraded API responses in EU-West".
incident-bot: Status page updated to: "Partial outage — degraded API responses in EU-West. Mitigations applied (traffic fallback). Investigating upstream TLS failures."
ops-rotation: ready to hand off to next oncall in 28m. leaving notes in runbook: `runbooks/edge_tls_handshake.md` -> steps 1-6 + rollback command.
megan_sre: follow-up: after reapplying previous cert bundle to primary pool, handshake errors dropped to baseline. promoting primary back over next 3m with gradual traffic shift.
dmitry_eng: confirmed rotation log showed an ordering bug in the new bundle (intermediate cert missing). filing PR to cert-roller: https://git.internal/redwood/cert-roller/pull/872
lia_support: customers informed of resolution and RCA will follow.
jamie_oncall: closing incident channel in 20m after postmortem draft. good job everyone. :tada:
